title: Promises
description: Promises represent eventual values — chain with .then, handle errors with .catch, run cleanup in .finally.

notes: Returning from .then becomes the next promise value; throwing inside .then becomes a rejection.
Without a .catch, an unhandled rejection just disappears (and warns in modern runtimes). Always terminate chains with .catch.
.finally is for cleanup — it does not receive the value or affect the resolved value.

questions.q: A rejected Promise is handled by:
What does throwing inside a .then callback do?
options: Becomes a rejected Promise the next .catch handles
After the Promise settles, either way

exercises.prompt: Resolve immediately with 42 and log the value.
Catch a rejection and log "caught" plus the message.

L3.prompt: Write `doubleAsync(x)` returning `Promise.resolve(x * 2)`. Call `doubleAsync(5)` and log the resolved value with .then.
hints: Promise.resolve(v) gives a Promise already fulfilled with v.
Use .then to receive the resolved value.
